A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HYPER++ research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original PPO experiments on ProcGen, DDQN experiments on Atari-5, and component, architecture, gradient, and target-update analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds PPG experiments on ProcGen, including aggregate scores, per-game results, and learning curves.

M1.justification: The core components and method equations remain unchanged. However, Figure 11 moves fixed 1/sqrt(d) scaling from before tanh to after it. Because v1's Equation 9 already specifies post-activation scaling, the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change or a diagram correction.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 16 ProcGen environments and five Atari games. PPG adds an algorithm setting on existing ProcGen coverage. Correcting the introduction's Atari-3 reference to Atari-5 does not add games; v1 already evaluates Atari-5.

E2.justification: The new PPG comparison evaluates Euclidean PPG and Hyper+S-RYM with PPG against HYPER++ with PPG (Figure 6 and Tables 13–14). The existing PPO and DDQN comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds a distinct PPG training and evaluation regime across ProcGen, including policy, value, and auxiliary phases with phase-specific epochs and behavior-cloning controls (Table 6). Existing PPO/DDQN settings remain unchanged. Table 9 also replaces the raw cross-game Avg summary with normalized IQM.

E4.justification: The component, normalization, latent-dimension, scaling, gradient, off-batch, and Polyak-update analyses retain their conditions and per-game results. Added IQM summaries change aggregate reporting, while the PPG comparison supplies additional benchmark evidence rather than a new ablation.

E5.justification: v2's Table 12 explicitly states that the existing architecture ablations average six seeds; v1's corresponding Table 11 does not specify this count. This is additional run-count disclosure, not evidence of additional runs. The established standard-deviation and bootstrap reporting practices are retained.

E6.justification: New PPG results include test IQM of 0.52 for HYPER++, 0.47 for Euclidean, and 0.34 for Hyper+S-RYM (Table 14), plus full train/test results and curves. Figure 1 changes HYPER++'s reported relative improvement from 28.9% to 52.3%, without explaining the revision. Existing per-game PPO and ablation values remain identical; normalized IQM summaries are added.

T1.justification: The gradient derivations, Lemma 4.1, Proposition 4.2, Corollary 4.3, and appendix proofs are retained. Correcting the matrix-size label accompanying Equation 6 from (1+s) to (1+d) does not change the displayed Jacobian or its derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit claim of transfer to PPG and revises the headline ProcGen return improvement from approximately 30% to 52%. The central gradient-instability diagnosis and three-component HYPER++ contribution remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix E.8 interpret the PPG findings as broader applicability, emphasizing that Hyper+S-RYM falls below the Euclidean baseline while HYPER++ retains an advantage. Existing mechanism explanations and the stated limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds PPG hyperparameters in Table 6 and identifies CleanRL defaults as their implementation basis. The reproducibility paragraph changes from a promised code release to stated public availability, although the same repository address already appears in v1's abstract.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for PPG, Matplotlib, and PyTorch and removes several introductory references, including Bolyai, Chami et al. (2019), Ouyang et al. (2022), and Silver et al. (2016). The substantive related-work discussion in Section 6 remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are rewritten and tightened, with smaller edits elsewhere, corrected cross-references, and removal of the author-contributions placeholder. Appendix PPO results are consolidated under one subsection, while the main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 6 replaces selected PPO curves with PPG aggregate results; the PPO curves remain available in the appendix. v2 adds PPG tables and learning-curve figures, redraws Figure 11's scaling sequence, and reorganizes existing tables with IQM summary rows and more consistent game ordering.

improvement.justification: The documented PPG comparisons strengthen evidence for applicability beyond v1's PPO/DDQN evaluations. The revised architecture diagram also agrees better with Equation 9, and aggregate table summaries improve accessibility. These are incremental gains; the unexplained change in Figure 1's headline percentage remains a reporting weakness.
